An AI agent is an LLM given the ability to take actions, not just generate text.

Choosing the right approach for grounding an LLM in your own data
The Core Difference
Both techniques solve the same underlying problem — an LLM trained on general internet text doesn't know your private documents, your company's latest data, or anything that happened after its training cutoff. Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and fine-tuning solve it in fundamentally different ways.
RAG leaves the model completely unchanged. Instead, it adds a retrieval step before generation: relevant chunks of your documents are found at query time and handed to the model as context, alongside the question. The model then answers from what it was just given, not from memory.
Fine-tuning changes the model itself. It continues the training process on a curated dataset, adjusting", "om what it was just given, not from memory.
Fine-tuning changes the model itself. It continues the training process on a curated dataset, adjusting the model's internal weights so that its default behavior shifts — toward a particular writing style, a domain vocabulary, or a specific task format.

Your source documents change frequently and you can't afford to retrain every time they do
You need to cite exactly where an answer came from — regulatory, legal, or trust requirements
